title: Atlas claim record
description: One claim: a single proposition, stated once, with what supports it (S06; D-044 to D-049, proposed). Staging claims live in data/staging/claims.json; accepted claims in data/claims.json (H-2). This file is the one home of the claim shape and of the claim-type, evidence-status, standing, review and search vocabularies. Why each value exists, how the MA §10 lists map onto them, the type × status table, the meaning of verified and the migration are in docs/architecture/claim-model.md. Claim type and evidence status are separate fields (L-06). There is no numeric confidence, score or rank (NG-11). Records point to claims through their claim_ids; a claim never lists the records it supports (D-044). Shared shapes come from entities.schema.json and sources.schema.json by $ref.

statement.description: The proposition, in the Atlas's words. It may not say more than the sentence at each cited locator (or than the input claims) supports.

citations.description: FACT and ATTRIBUTION only: the sources that state the proposition, each at one locator.

input_claim_ids.description: DERIVATION, INTERPRETATION and IMPLICATION only: the claims this one rests on. Sources are reached through them, never cited directly.

reasoning.description: DERIVATION, INTERPRETATION and IMPLICATION only: the step from the inputs to the statement, naming the rule or choice applied (e.g. ER-1, a TQ answer).

as_of.description: FACT and ATTRIBUTION only: the date the content describes, when the source says it (source-policy.md §12). not_stated otherwise; the source's own dates then apply. A claim with inputs takes its dates from them, so it has none.

verified_on.description: When the Verifier last checked this claim (D-048). Required unless the status is unverified, forbidden when it is. Per record, never a batch stamp (L-06).

disputed_with.description: disputed only: the competing claims. They stay in the record; a disputed status never replaces them (D-046).

review.description: The human's class C review (CLAUDE.md §9). Only an accepted claim may be canonical (D-048).

citation.description: One source at one locator. The anchor is a verbatim extract of the sentence (or table cell) that states the proposition; the locator says where that sentence is. The Verifier and the human judge the claim against that sentence (D-047).

locator.description: PDF page index (p.N) or, for HTML, the section heading and the sentence's opening words.

anchor.description: Verbatim, including the source's own quotation marks and apostrophes.

originator.description: reporter citations only: the first link of the attribution chain, as the retrieved source names it (source-policy.md §4, ER-6). The originator was not retrieved and is never cited as if it had been.

source_class.description: The class the originator's statement would have, read from how the reporter describes it (an INTERPRETATION, because the originator was not read).

named_at.description: Where in the retrieved source the originator is named.

read.description: The bytes the Verifier read to check this citation. When the hash differs from the source record's retrieval, the source changed and the anchor was re-checked (source-policy.md §12).

search.description: DERIVATION only: the search record ER-3 requires before a value may be not_publicly_determinable (D-049). Whether the classes searched are every preferred class of the citing record's matrix row is checked where the row is known, on the record (V-10 family, S10).

gap.description: not_accessible only: what refused access, and when.

state_not_stated.description: The source gives no as-of date for this content.

state_not_reviewed.description: The human has not reviewed this claim. It cannot be canonical.

reviewer.description: Class C review is the human's (CLAUDE.md §9). No agent role may write a verdict.

recorded_in.description: The session report whose addendum holds the human's words.

vocab_claim_type.description: CLAUDE.md §6 labels, written as CLAUDE.md writes them. MA §10's seven types map onto these five (claim-model.md §2).

oneOf.description: A proposition about the world, stated by a first-hand source (standing party or originator) at its locator. Never the Atlas's own inference.
What a named source says, defines, claims, plans or estimates, recorded as that source's statement. Superlatives, intentions and second-hand reports are always this type (ER-5, ER-6, ER-8).
A proposition that follows from other claims, or from a recorded search, by a stated step. The Atlas's inference, shown as inferred.
The Atlas's own judgement or choice, such as a working definition, citing the claims it interprets.
A consequence for the Atlas's research, data or users, drawn from the claims it cites. Not a forecast about the world.

vocab_evidence_status.description: How well the evidence supports the claim, after verification (D-046). Not a claim type and not a confidence value. Only supported and disputed claims may be canonical.

oneOf.description: No Verifier has checked this claim yet. Written explicitly, never a default.

The Verifier read each cited locator, found the anchor, and judged that the sentence states the proposition and the wording does not exceed it; for a claim with inputs, every input is supported and the stated step follows. MA §10 'direct', renamed.
The anchors or inputs were found but support only part of the proposition: the wording exceeds them. The claim must be narrowed into a new claim before any record rests on it.
The cited locators were read and do not state the proposition. At most they give context, and the claim supports no record (ER-10).

Supported by its own evidence, and in factual contradiction with other supported claims, named in disputed_with (source-policy.md §10.1). Never used for definitional, wording, temporal or scope conflicts.

vocab_standing.description: How the publisher relates to this claim (D-035). The values' meanings are source-policy.md §4.

oneOf.description: source-policy.md §4, row reporter. Needs the originator (ER-6) and supports at most ATTRIBUTION.
The human accepts the claim as canonical. It moves to data/claims.json.
The human rejects the claim. It stays in staging with this verdict, so the evidence is not lost.
Sources of this class were read for the question, and none states the answer.
Sources of this class could not be read (source-policy.md §11). The class was not searched, so the conclusion can be at most not_researched (ER-3, SP-7).
